author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. The correction updates that visit in place, never adding another, and is reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is opened, then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) shows that visit's current date and description in its `visit` model attribute

given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are POSTed to the same URL, then that visit is updated in place, the pet gains no additional visit, and the response redirects to the owner detail page
given a blank description, when a correction is POSTed, then the correction is refused, the form is redisplayed, and the description field carries the error
given a date of today or earlier, when a correction is POSTed, then the correction is refused, the form is redisplayed, and the date field carries the error
edge case 3: correcting a visit through a pet that does not belong to the named owner is refused
edge case 4: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or that does not exist, is refused
non_goals: an edit link or any other entry point on the owner detail page (owner decision: reachable by URL alone in this request)
a different validation rule for correcting visits whose date has passed
notes: PRD and ADR edits are already in the working tree: NG-5 narrowed to cancellation, REQ-VIS-003 added to Visits with edge cases 3-4, new non-goal ADR 2026-11-04-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, 2026-08-08 ADR status amended, ADR index updated. The implementation surface is the controller and its tests. Open points recorded as narrowest readings: (1) correction validates exactly like booking, so a past-dated visit can be corrected only by moving its date into the future; this is recorded as a PRD Open Question, with no special rule built. (2) Mismatched owner/pet/visit ids and unknown visits are refused, matching how booking already refuses a pet of another owner (REQ-VIS-001 edge case 1); the request did not state this. (3) The success flash message wording is left to design; keep it translated per REQ-LANG-002. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the visit-side twin of the existing pet edit flow (PetController.findPet with an optional path id; updatePetDetails in place). It stays inside the owner aggregate: Owner -> getPet(petId) -> Pet.getVisit(visitId), persisted through OwnerRepository only (system-design.md § Contracts, invariants note; § Overview). Adjustments: (1) Pet gains a lookup of one persisted visit by identifier, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer); (2) VisitController's class-wide @ModelAttribute("visit") loader branches on an optional visitId path variable: absent keeps today's behavior (new Visit attached to the pet), present returns the existing visit and attaches nothing, refusing an unknown or foreign visit with IllegalArgumentException exactly as it refuses a foreign pet; (3) the correction confirmation is resolved from the message bundles in the request locale; (4) a new § Scale and Load row covers the id-resolution path. NG-5 narrowing is recorded by the PRD expert's non-goal ADR; no design-side ADR needed. Basis: grep of src/main/java (IDE oracle not connected), the weaker basis.
integration_points: Entry points GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController, rendering pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm (the form has no th:action, so it posts back to the same URL) and redirecting to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success.

Binding target for the correction POST: the persisted Visit resolved from the path by the loader, behind an allow-list of exactly date and description (setAllowedFields on the visit binder), keeping the existing id and *.id disallow list (security-principles.md § mass assignment row; system-design.md § Threat Model). The persisted Visit is never bound whole. Scoping the allow-list to the "visit" binder is preferred; if the class-wide binder carries it, booking narrows to the same two fields with no observable change.

Repository boundary in tests: OwnerRepository via the class's existing @MockitoBean stub (testing-principles.md § mocking: tolerated). Reason: the @WebMvcTest context already registers it for the whole class; a second hand-written double in the same slice context would conflict. Fixture: extend the @BeforeEach owner/pet with a persisted visit (id set), and assert no additional visit via the pet's visit count and the updated fields on that same Visit instance.
Framework transport in tests: MockMvc, the sanctioned double (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Message bundles: one new confirmation key added to every bundle under src/main/resources/messages/ (eleven locales), resolved through the injected MessageSource with the handler's Locale argument (REQ-LANG-001 locale resolver). The REQ-LANG-002 bundle-key test then guards completeness.

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute loader with @PathVariable(required = false) id: absent creates, present resolves the persisted child
lookup of a persisted child by identifier, skipping new instances, returning null when absent; Pet.getVisit mirrors it
non-future date check rejecting with typeMismatch.visitDate, then save through OwnerRepository and redirect

risks.risk: Phantom visit: the class-wide loader today attaches a new Visit to the pet on every request; on the edit route, cascade save would insert it and the pet would gain an additional visit.
risks.mitigation: The loader attaches a new Visit only when visitId is absent (system-design.md § Contracts invariants note: Visit persisted only through cascade from Owner). The in-place test asserts the pet's visit count is unchanged.

risks.risk: Business rule placement: the non-future-date check is a controller-held rule (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; recorded deviation). A second copy would widen the deviation.
risks.mitigation: Both handlers call one shared check in VisitController, so the correction applies the existing rule rather than adding a rule. Resolving the visit from the path is address binding, not a business rule; the lookup itself lives on Pet.

risks.risk: Refusal of a foreign or unknown visit leaks detail through the error page, which renders exception messages (system-design.md § Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: The exception message carries identifiers only, as the existing pet refusal does, never data values (security-principles.md § secret disclosure row).

risks.risk: Path scaling with data: visit resolution scans one pet's visits after one owner load (system-design.md § Scale and Load, owner-graph row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: linear scan of the eagerly fetched collection; no new query.

risks.risk: A failed correction leaves the bound values on the detached Visit instance.
risks.mitigation: Nothing is saved on the error path (architecture-principles.md § Design Principles 7, fail secure); the instance is discarded with the request.

notes: Design doc writes: Contracts rows for Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, VisitController now cite REQ-VIS-003; new § Scale and Load section (doctor template) with the owner-graph resolution row; Security Context inputs name visit identifiers; Threat Model mass-assignment row names the correction allow-list; Known Defects gains a derived, unconfirmed row: flash success and error messages in OwnerController, PetController, and VisitController booking are fixed English, invisible to the template-walking REQ-LANG-002 test. That row is not fixed by this slice; only the new correction confirmation is translated. Out of scope and not required: the form's submit button reads the addVisit label on the correction form too (template not in file_targets). No design-doc-autofix records to audit. The uncommitted ADR changes (2026-11-04 non-goal ADR, 2026-08-08 status amendment, ADR README index) are the product-requirements-expert's per the prd-entry notes; this dispatch did not write them.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit holds its own decision path (`!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)`: a not-yet-saved visit is never matched, an absent id returns null). docs/system-design.md row 90 assigns Pet the role 'resolves one of its persisted visits by identifier', so the rule sits below the controller boundary, yet it is exercised only through the @WebMvcTest in VisitControllerTests (ls of the owner test dir shows no PetTests; `grep getVisit src/test` found no unit caller). Dropping the `!visit.isNew()` guard fails no test, because every controller case uses a persisted id. Per the pyramid this belongs in a plain unit test at the Pet seam.
findings.fix: Add a PetTests unit test (no framework) named in the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school: the pet should return the persisted visit with the given id, return null for an unknown id, and never match a visit that has no id. The controller tests keep one representative path.

findings.description: The allow-list `setAllowedFields("date", "description")` is the design's mass-assignment guard for the persisted Visit (the design-block names it as the security-principles mass-assignment mitigation). No test posts an extra field. Deleting the @InitBinder("visit") method leaves all 7 new tests green (the correction test sends only date and description), though it would let a request overwrite the persisted visit's other bound fields. A plausible change would break this guard and no test would notice.
findings.fix: Add one test: a correction POST that also carries a disallowed field (e.g. a pet or id parameter named by role) leaves that field on bookedVisit unchanged while date and description update.

recommendations: The correction success test does not assert the flash `message` ('visitCorrected' key resolved through MessageSource with the request Locale); a change that dropped the confirmation would pass. Optional: add flash().attribute assertion.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership scoping (edge cases 3 and 4): the correction resolves owner, then pet through owner.getPet, then visit through the new Pet.getVisit, which filters `!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)` (Pet.java, added hunk); a visit id belonging to another pet or owner resolves to null and findVisit throws, so no cross-owner IDOR. Covered by VisitControllerTests.java:169 `theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAPetOfAnotherOwner`, :177 `...ForAVisitOfAnotherPet`, :192 `...ForAnUnknownVisit`.

Mass assignment: the bound target on the edit route is the persisted Visit, and the change adds `@InitBinder("visit")` with `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description")` on top of the retained global `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (VisitController.java:58-61), so neither the visit id nor its pet linkage can be bound; the owner attribute on the update handler is `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, so the form's hidden `petId` input (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html) binds nowhere.

Validation on every persisting path: processUpdateVisitForm takes `@Valid Visit visit` (description @NotBlank in Visit.java) and runs the shared rejectNonFutureDate before `this.owners.save(owner)`; the date rule is extracted, not weakened, on the create path.

Cross-request state: the @ModelAttribute loader re-reads owner, pet, and visit from the repository on every request (spring.jpa.open-in-view=false in application.properties, so the save merges a freshly loaded graph); nothing trusts an earlier request's resolution.

Data access: the only write is the existing OwnerRepository.save; no query text is composed. Error messages added in findVisit carry only integer path ids, no sensitive values, into the error page that renders `${message}` (error.html:18).

Output escaping: no template changed; createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit/pet values via th:text only. The flash message comes from MessageSource key visitCorrected (messages*.properties, static text, no request-derived argument).

Exposed surface: one new GET and one POST under /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, mutating only the named visit's date and description, open like every route by the demonstration baseline (security-principles.md § Standing Gaps: no authn/authz/CSRF); no management exposure change.

Secrets: grep of added diff lines for password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential (case-insensitive) matched only a system-design.md prose line about datasource credentials from environment variables; no credential added.

Supply chain: build.gradle and gradle/ unchanged (`git diff --stat -- build.gradle gradle` empty); no dependency scan runs, a listed standing gap; resolved runtimeClasspath shows spring-boot 4.1.2, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.7, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE; no NVD match run in this review.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Contained to the owner package: Pet gains one lookup and VisitController gains one GET and one POST route, plus one bundle key in each of the eleven locales and docs edits. No sensitive paths. The new routes are an unauthenticated write route on the declared security surface, which the round-1 security review covered and which matches the project's standing demonstration baseline.

semantic_surprise.note: The persistence logic is sound: cascade ALL on Owner.pets and Pet.visits merges the bound visit in place, and ownership scoping and the date rule are extracted, not weakened. The reused template does surprise in two ways. Because the form binds straight onto the persisted visit, a refused correction redraws the Previous Visits table (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:51) with the rejected values as that visit's row. The correction form's submit button still reads Add Visit (line 39). The class-wide visit allow-list also narrows the booking binder, which has no observable effect today.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real. MockMvc drives every Done-when bullet and edge cases 3 and 4. They assert the same visit instance, the unchanged visit count, save called or never called, and the field-error codes. PetTests covers the isNew guard. Residual gaps: the in-place update is checked only against a mocked repository, so no test exercises the JPA merge, and the allow-list test would pass without the allow-list.

reviewer_hedging.note: All dispatched reviewers approved with citations, and the security review is from round 1 because the fix-delta plan scoped it out. The late-round approvals carry recommendations. The test-reviewer states the allow-list test is tautological given the global id disallow and was not verified by mutation. The code-quality reviewer parks a null-versus-Optional return on Pet.getVisit.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations, or build retries. The diff matches the intake: the edit routes, reuse of the template, the update in place, the redirect to the owner, no edit link, and the NG-5 narrowing recorded in a new ADR. The fix-round delta was tests and docs only. The open questions on past visits and an entry point are recorded in the PRD, not decided silently.

rationale: Correct and well scoped, but the reused form has two display surprises a test cannot catch. A refused correction redraws the visit history with the rejected values, and the button reads Add Visit. Read VisitController's update path and the template together. Then decide whether the tautological allow-list test and the history redraw are acceptable for this slice.
